title: C16 · The client's door, and the email they never have to send
anchor: Client portal and reorder shop, feature inventory 8 August 2026; tracking surfaced to the portal in daily use

slides.headline: THE EMAIL YOUR CLIENT NEVER HAS TO SEND
slides.sub: A client should not have to ask a human where their own order is.
slides.boundary: Demo tenant throughout. No real client, no real order.

lede: It is the most common question in this business and the least interesting work in it. Somebody reads an email, opens three screens, copies a tracking number, and writes a reply that says in transit.
The client did not want a reply. They wanted the answer.
slides.boundary: Answering it used to take three screens on my side.

items.text: Live jobs, with the status ladder from brief through delivered
Past orders, so a reorder starts from what they actually bought
Carrier and tracking on the job, the moment it exists
Messages on the specific job, not a shared inbox thread
A proof to approve, on a link with no login to remember

slides.boundary: A link plus a company password. No seat to buy, no app to install.

left.p: What did we order last time, do you still have the art, what did it cost, can you send a quote.

right.p: A catalogue of what that client has already bought. The cart becomes a real quote on my side, with the artwork already attached.

slides.boundary: No login on the reorder shop by design. Friction is how reorders die.

slides.label: at a six minute median, because approving a proof is one link and two buttons.
slides.sub: The suite that asked people to log in and hunt for the file died at zero rows across six tables.
slides.boundary: Every decision writes a receipt with a name and a time on it.

items.text: Your cost, your supplier, your margin, ever
Any other client, any other job, any other contact
Internal notes, team discussion, the pipeline
Files from a public link, every bucket is private and served to a session
The portal is read mostly, so a client cannot edit your record

slides.boundary: A receipt goes out with no money on it, and physically cannot carry any.

lede: The portal and the reorder shop are built and working, and they have not been handed to a client book yet.

Two things are open before they are. Somebody has to be told when a client messages a job nobody owns, and the order totals in the portal need to come from the invoice rather than a summary. Both are on the page, in writing, where the team can read them.
slides.boundary: Built, not yet handed over. Said plainly on purpose.

slides.quote: Nothing leaves the building without a person. Six systems in here write email, and not one of them can press send.
slides.src: Which is also why your client never gets a status update that turned out to be a guess.
slides.boundary: No automated message has ever reached a client from this platform unsent by a human.

slides.h2: WANT THE DOOR ON YOUR OWN BOOK
lede: Access is by request. I will stand it up against your own jobs and let you click it before you decide anything.
slides.boundary: Demo tenant for the walkthrough. Your book stays yours.
